pairs.subject: browser-credential-boundary
pairs.evidence: scripts/onboard-ui/server.mjs:236 The wizard server acts with the person's ambient Claude CLI login and writes .env.local. It binds to 127.0.0.1, but its request handler never checks the Host, forwarded-host, Origin or forwarded-for headers before routing, so the only gate is the per-run token. The technique requires that header gate in addition to the bind and treats neither as optional.

techniques.evidence: scripts/onboard-ui/server.mjs:263 The bind half is in place (line 467 listens on 127.0.0.1). There is no Host, X-Forwarded-Host, Origin or forwarded-for refusal: Origin is used only to grant CORS. A DNS-rebound page reaches the token-free static routes. The per-run token blocks the mutating routes and /events, which in practice covers rebinding, but the technique names the token as a complement to the header gate, not a substitute. No test pins the loopback bind.

scripts/onboard-ui/server.mjs:310 The /app proxy relays err.message and, at line 307, passes the upstream status through unchanged; the comment there makes this a deliberate choice. Severity is low because the caller holds the token and is the machine owner, but this is the failure the technique names.

scripts/onboard-ui/server.mjs:340 Pending card state, including which env name a secret goes to, is kept server-side and the client sends back only a card id, so nothing the server produced comes back needing a seal.

scripts/onboard-ui/engine.mjs:1179 The app proxy attaches no credential. It exists for cost control: paths are enumerated and the body is rebuilt from validated fields with sample text the server chooses. No privileged secret is involved.

pairs.registryProposal: loopback-addressed-request-gate could say explicitly how to judge a server that binds to loopback and requires a CSPRNG per-run capability token on every state-changing route but has no Host check. Today the technique calls the header gate mandatory and positions a per-session credential as a complement, so a token-only design is a deviation even though the token defeats rebinding for every route that acts. Stating the residual (token-free static routes and topology readable under a rebound name) would make the verdict less arguable.
